questions.question:
D1 — Review focus
Project/branch/task: User Dashboard plan on main, design review.
ELI10: I rated this plan 4/10 for design completeness. The biggest gaps are: no visual hierarchy or layout per screen size, no real copy or actions for the empty/loading/error states, and no design system (fonts, colors, spacing). Next I'll make visual mockups, then go through all 7 design areas. You can narrow the review to a few areas instead.
Stakes if we pick wrong: if we narrow too far, unreviewed gaps such as accessibility or responsive layout get decided ad hoc during the build.
Recommendation: A because the plan is thin on design across the board, and a full pass costs minutes.
Completeness: A=10/10, B=6/10
Pros / cons:
A) All 7 areas (recommended)
  ✅ Covers hierarchy, states, journey, slop risk, design system, responsive and a11y
  ✅ Every gap gets its own decision before anyone writes code
  ❌ More questions to answer, about one per open gap across the passes
B) Only the areas I name
  ✅ Faster, with fewer decisions in the parts you care most about
  ✅ Lets you skip areas you plan to cover in another review
  ❌ Areas you skip go unreviewed and get decided ad hoc later
Net: full coverage at the cost of more questions, vs speed with blind spots.

options.label: All 7 areas (recommended)
options.description: ✅ Covers every design dimension. ✅ Each gap gets its own decision. ❌ More questions to answer.

options.label: Only specific areas
options.description: ✅ Faster, fewer decisions. ✅ Skip areas covered elsewhere. ❌ Skipped areas go unreviewed.

questions.question:
Want outside design voices before the detailed review?
D2 — Outside design voices
Project/branch/task: User Dashboard plan on main, design review.
ELI10: Before the 7 passes I can bring in two extra reviewers. Codex checks the plan against hard design rules and a litmus scorecard. A separate Claude agent does a fresh completeness read. That cross-checks my judgment, but it takes longer.
Stakes if we pick wrong: skipping means every finding rests on one reviewer; running it adds a few minutes.
Recommendation: B because there are no mockups to anchor a scorecard and the gaps here are mostly missing specs, which one reviewer can list.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Pros / cons:
A) Yes, run outside design voices
  ✅ Codex hard-rule + litmus scorecard plus an independent Claude completeness read
  ✅ Disagreements surface with both perspectives in the relevant pass
  ❌ Adds a few minutes; Codex may be missing here, in which case only the Claude voice runs
B) No, proceed without (recommended)
  ✅ Straight into the 7 passes with the plan as the anchor
  ✅ Fewest steps to a fixed plan
  ❌ Findings rest on one reviewer; no cross-model check on slop risk or hierarchy
Net: a cross-model check vs getting to the fixed plan sooner.

options.label: Yes, run outside design voices
options.description: ✅ Codex hard-rule + litmus scorecard plus an independent Claude completeness read. ✅ Disagreements surface with both perspectives in the relevant pass. ❌ Adds a few minutes; Codex may be missing here, in which case only the Claude voice runs and it's tagged single-model.

options.label: No, proceed without (recommended)
options.description: ✅ Straight into the 7 passes with the approved mockup as anchor. ✅ Fewest steps to a fixed plan. ❌ Findings rest on one reviewer; no cross-model check on slop risk or hierarchy.

questions.question:
D3 — Cross-project learnings
Project/branch/task: User Dashboard plan on main, design review.
ELI10: gstack can search what it learned in your other projects on this machine for patterns that might apply here. It stays local; no data leaves your machine. This project has no learnings yet, so the search found nothing here.
Stakes if we pick wrong: enabling it on client work can carry one client's patterns into another's review.
Recommendation: A because for a solo developer, past pitfalls from other repos often apply here.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Pros / cons:
A) Enable cross-project learnings (recommended)
  ✅ Reviews can reuse pitfalls and patterns you already hit in other repos
  ✅ Stays fully local, and you can switch it off later with gstack-config
  ❌ Patterns from unrelated client codebases could leak into this review
B) Keep learnings project-scoped only
  ✅ No cross-contamination between separate client codebases on this machine
  ✅ Review evidence comes only from this repo and this conversation
  ❌ Lessons from your other projects never surface here
Net: more reusable insight vs strict isolation between codebases.

options.label: Enable cross-project (recommended)
options.description: ✅ Reuse pitfalls from other repos. ✅ Local only, reversible. ❌ Client patterns could cross over.

options.label: Project-scoped only
options.description: ✅ No cross-contamination. ✅ Evidence from this repo only. ❌ Other projects' lessons never surface.

questions.question:
D4 — Issue 1: what does the user see first?
Project/branch/task: User Dashboard plan on main, Pass 1 Information Architecture.
ELI10: The plan lists Activity, Notifications and Quick actions but not their order or relative size. Without a ranking, the engineer gives each panel equal weight and the user's eye has nowhere to land. We need to pick the primary region.
Stakes if we pick wrong: users skim past unread items or hunt for the way back to work, and the dashboard turns into a page people bounce off.
Recommendation: 1A because unread notifications are the only thing here that needs action, and the 'Hierarchy as service' principle says the actionable item goes first.
Completeness: A=10/10, B=9/10, C=7/10
Pros / cons:
A) Notifications-first (recommended)
  ✅ Page header holds the greeting, unread-count line and both quick actions inline, so 'back to work' is one click from the top
  ✅ lg: Notifications in the wide left column (about 7/12), Activity on the right (5/12); below lg they stack Notifications, then Activity
  ❌ Users who come mainly to review their own recent edits scroll past notifications first
B) Activity-first
  ✅ Activity in the wide main column, Notifications as a right sidebar; suits a team that mostly checks its own history
  ✅ Same inline-header quick actions as A
  ❌ Unread items move to a narrow sidebar, and on mobile they sit below a long feed
C) Single column for all sizes
  ✅ Simplest build: header, Notifications, Activity in one reading column at every width
  ✅ No column-width or balance decisions to make for lg
  ❌ Wastes wide screens and puts Activity far below the fold on desktop
Net: lead with what needs action (A), with personal history (B), or with simplicity (C).

options.label: 1A Notifications-first (recommended)
options.description: Header with greeting and inline quick actions; lg 7/12 Notifications + 5/12 Activity; stacks N then A below lg.

options.label: 1B Activity-first
options.description: Activity in the main column, Notifications as a right sidebar; same header.

options.label: 1C Single column
options.description: Header, Notifications, Activity in one column at every width.
